location: Iowa, USA (4 sites: Ames, Crawfordsville, Lewis, Nashua)
comparison: rye cover crop vs. no cover crop, no-till corn-soybean rotation
metric: corn grain yield reduction at economic optimum N rate (EONR)
quote: The RCC reduced corn grain yield by 6% at the economic optimum N rate (EONR).
note: Negative effect: yield lower with RCC. YEONR 12.20 (no-RCC) vs 11.41 Mg/ha (RCC), Table 5.

comparison: rye cover crop vs. no cover crop, no-till corn-soybean rotation
metric: corn grain yield difference at EONR (no-RCC minus RCC)
quote: Also, the YEONR was 6% (0.79 Mg ha-1) greater with no-RCC than RCC (Table 5).
note: Yield lower with RCC by 0.79 Mg/ha; EONR 181 vs 185 kg N/ha (no-RCC vs RCC).

comparison: rye cover crop vs. no cover crop, averaged across six N rates (0-225 kg N ha-1)
metric: corn grain yield difference across N rates (no-RCC minus RCC)
quote: Across N rates, average corn grain yield was greater with no-RCC than RCC (0.95 Mg ha-1; P < 0.001; Table 4, Fig. 2b), and was 0.75 Mg ha-1 greater at the agronomic maximum N rate (plateau yield; Table 5).
note: Yield lower with RCC. In the extracted text 'no-RCC' is split across a line break as 'no-' / 'RCC'; rejoined here as 'no-RCC'.

comparison: rye cover crop vs. no cover crop, at agronomic maximum N rate
metric: corn plateau grain yield difference (no-RCC minus RCC)
quote: Across N rates, average corn grain yield was greater with no-RCC than RCC (0.95 Mg ha-1; P < 0.001; Table 4, Fig. 2b), and was 0.75 Mg ha-1 greater at the agronomic maximum N rate (plateau yield; Table 5).
note: Plateau yields 12.21 (no-RCC) vs 11.46 Mg/ha (RCC), Table 5. Same line-break rejoin of 'no-RCC' as E3.
